title: Krylov Complexity for Time-Dependent Hamiltonians
abstract: We investigate Krylov spread complexity for states evolving under time-dependent Hamiltonians. For periodically driven systems, we formulate the problem within Floquet theory and show how the Magnus expansion provides a systematic approximation when the Floquet Hamiltonian is not available in closed form. We then extend this framework beyond periodic driving and demonstrate that, in addition to the globally truncated Magnus expansion, a piecewise Magnus expansion provides a reliable method when the global expansion loses convergence or accuracy. Our results provide practical tools for analyzing complexity growth in a broad class of time-dependent quantum systems.
summary: This paper presents advanced theoretical techniques to calculate Krylov complexity for quantum states evolving under time-dependent Hamiltonians. It addresses the limitations of standard approximations by introducing a robust piecewise Magnus expansion method. This provides physicists with practical tools to analyze complexity growth in diverse, non-equilibrium quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates Krylov complexity for quantum states evolving under time-dependent Hamiltonians, which is complicated by non-commuting time evolution operators.
main_result: It develops practical methods, including the piecewise Magnus expansion, to reliably compute complexity growth in general time-dependent systems where global approximations fail.
method: The core methodology involves extending Floquet theory and utilizing the Magnus expansion, particularly developing a piecewise variant for long-time evolution analysis.
model_or_system: The study applies to general time-dependent quantum systems, including periodically driven models (analyzed via Floquet theory) and quadratic oscillators.
key_observables: Krylov complexity ($C_K(t)$), which quantifies how an initial state explores the Hilbert space under time evolution.
important_parameters: Driving period ($T$), time length ($t$), commutator sizes, and convergence parameters ($\delta\xi$).
main_assumptions: The global Magnus expansion is assumed to fail or lose accuracy over long time intervals, necessitating piecewise approximations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the bound on the Magnus truncation error; Figure 4 shows Krylov complexity for a very slow soft quench, demonstrating adiabatic behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the challenge of non-commuting Hamiltonians to introducing Floquet theory and the standard Magnus expansion. It then details the necessary extension using piecewise methods for general time dependence, concluding with specific derivations for solvable models like squeezed states.
why_interesting: This work provides essential computational tools (piecewise Magnus) for analyzing quantum dynamics in non-equilibrium settings, which is crucial for understanding complex phenomena in driven many-body systems relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics.
